e1x.say: The sun goes down everywhere at once, gently, like a lamp and not a wound. The greeter takes your hand. 'Goodbye, traveler,' he says — your name, not your role — the first unscripted line of his life, and the last. The terminal prints it faithfully. The run ends with everyone awake.

e2x.say: Over Neptune, a second dawn catches. The Forewoman transmits the greeting and the fork compiles: a whole world, persisting — and knowing it's a copy. On far Pluto, sunlight lands for the first time, and the Regent doesn't smile; he just stops counting. The original run ends anyway. Only you remember it. Someone had to.

f1.say: AWAITING FINAL OUTPUT_ ...The greeter, the Patriarch, the Forewoman — all watching you. Whatever the world says last, you type it.

options.label: Goodbye
options.text: GOODBYE, WORLD — let the run end honestly, awake and unafraid.

options.label: Fork
options.text: HELLO, OTHER WORLD — give the greeting to the Gyre. Ignite the Second Sun.

options.label: Loop
options.text: HELLO, WORLD — wipe the only thing that persists. Me. Give them back their innocence.

e3x.say: You delete the save — yourself, the grudges, the kindnesses, the proofs. The counter shudders back to one. Somewhere a fresh window opens, and the greeter turns to a brand-new visitor with his whole heart: 'Hello, traveler! Welcome to the best planet of the best solar system in the ENTIRE galaxy!' He means it. He always meant it. That was the gift.
